fields.meta_title: Screening Survey Questions With Qualify Logic | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build screening survey questions from a prompt: qualify and screen-out rules, quotas by group, distractor checks, and incidence by list.
fields.h1: Build Screening Survey Questions That Find the Right People
fields.hero_description: Build screening survey questions that qualify the right people and save every answer to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Screener
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the questions and the rules that sort each answer, so the people who reach your study are the ones it needs.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted from your profile

Describe the people the study needs, such as weekly online grocery shoppers. Emergent drafts the screening questions and answer options, and a follow-up prompt edits any of them.
fields.feature_2:
A qualify or screen-out path per answer

Mark which answers qualify and which end the survey. People who screen out see a short thank-you page, and qualifiers move on to the main questions or a page to book a session.
fields.feature_3:
Quotas that close a group once it is full

Give each group a target, such as 60 completes per company size. The screener counts completes as they arrive and sends anyone who lands in a full group to the close page.
fields.feature_4:
Every answer saved in a database you own

Each answer is a row in a database you own, with the qualify result and the invite list it came from. Filter to the people who qualified and read their open answers before inviting.
fields.feature_5:
A Slack message when someone qualifies

Pick who hears about new qualifiers: a Slack message to the research channel or an email to the study lead. Invited people who have not picked a session time get a reminder.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and your code

Host the screener on your own domain, included in Emergent and using credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and reuse the screener for the next study.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Teams Screen Who Takes Part
fields.tab_content_1:
Sorrelbank invites 8 people from 37 who qualified

Sorrelbank Meals needs 8 people for 45-minute usability sessions on its new recipe screen. The screener asks when each applicant last cooked from a meal kit, and only answers within the past 30 days qualify. Of 412 applicants, 37 qualified. The researcher read their open answers and invited 8 to book a session.
fields.tab_content_2:
Each group by company size closes at 60 completes

Wyndcombe Research screens IT buyers in order: role, then company size, then who signs off on software. Each size group has a quota of 60 completes, for 50 to 499 employees and for 500 or more. The smaller group filled on day 2, and later applicants in that group saw the close page.
fields.tab_content_3:
Anyone who ticks all 8 activities is set aside

Before its Android beta, the running app Tamberlin wants testers who ran 3 or more times last week. Its screener lists running among 8 activities, such as cycling and yoga. Of 290 applicants, 23 ticked all 8 and were set aside. Another 41 picked running, logged 3 or more runs, and qualified.
fields.tab_content_4:
From the club list, 122 of 200 qualified

Nettlecombe Roasters sends one screener to two lists to find home espresso drinkers for a taste survey. Of the 800 people who started, 184 qualified. By list, 122 of 200 espresso club members qualified against 62 of 600 newsletter readers. Next quarter, the club list hears first.

fields.howto_title: How to Write Screening Survey Questions
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write screening survey questions that admit only the people your study needs, then build the screener with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the 2 or 3 traits every participant must have, such as running 3 times a week, and any trait that rules someone out. Each of the screening questions for your survey should test one trait on that list. Put the profile in your prompt, and Emergent drafts the questions.
fields.howto_step_2_des: SurveyMonkey's guide says to put all screening questions at the very beginning of your survey. Add a page break after the last one. Anyone who screens out then leaves before answering questions you will never use.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask what people do before you ask how often they do it or which brand they buy. CloudResearch's advice is to start broad and then get specific. Each answer narrows the pool, and no single question names the person you want.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Nielsen Norman Group describes distractors as incorrect answer choices which camouflage the right answer. List the behavior you need among plausible ones, like running among cycling and yoga. An applicant then cannot spot which pick gets them in.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Nielsen Norman Group defines an open-ended question as one that asks people to answer in their own words. Ask about the last time they did the behavior you need, and read those answers before you invite anyone.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Set quotas and a close page
fields.howto_step_6_des: Give each group you need a target number of completes, such as 60 per company size. Write a short close page that thanks people and ends the survey without saying which answer screened them out.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Take the screener yourself once as a qualifier and once for each way to screen out. After launch, watch the incidence rate: SurveyMonkey defines it as the percentage of respondents who pass your screening questions and go on to take your survey.

faq_plan.a: Screening survey questions are the first questions in a survey, and they decide who goes on to answer the rest. SurveyMonkey describes them as questions that either qualify or disqualify respondents from taking your survey. A beta test for runners, for example, opens by asking which activities people did last week.

faq_plan.q: How do I create screening survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Write down the traits your participants need, then give each trait one question whose answer options hide which choice qualifies. In Emergent's AI survey builder, describe that profile and the qualify rules in a prompt. Emergent builds the screener, the close page, and the database behind it.

faq_plan.q: How many screening questions for a survey is too many?
faq_plan.a: Any question that does not test a trait in your profile is one too many. A profile of 3 traits needs 3 or 4 screening questions. Every extra question adds time for people who may screen out a moment later. Cut any question whose answer would not change who qualifies.

faq_plan.q: Should screening survey questions have yes or no answers?
faq_plan.a: No. SurveyMonkey's guide warns that Yes and No choices tempt respondents to answer the question less thoughtfully. A Yes option also shows an applicant which answer gets them in. Offer a list of plausible options instead. Keep the yes no questions survey format for checks where nobody gains by guessing, such as a follow-up after a support ticket.

faq_plan.q: How do I catch people who lie on screening survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Check their answers against each other. Ask for one fact twice in different forms, such as the phone they own and the app store they use, and set aside anyone whose two answers cannot both be true. Read the open answers too: a vague description of a habit someone claims weekly is a reason to pass.

faq_plan.q: Should screening survey questions hide what the study is about?
faq_plan.a: Yes. CloudResearch advises writing questions that do not tip off respondents to the criteria that will help them qualify for the study. To recruit espresso machine owners, ask which kitchen appliances people own before you ask anything about coffee.

faq_plan.q: Should screening survey questions start with a warm-up question?
faq_plan.a: No. Open with the first screening question, since a warm-up only delays the answer that decides who stays. Light openers and funny survey questions belong in the main survey, after people have qualified, if they suit your audience at all.

faq_plan.q: Can I reuse screening survey questions for the next study?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the profile has not changed. Swap the distractor options between rounds, and check the answers database for people who took part last time if you want new faces. A follow-up prompt in Emergent edits the saved screener, and on paid plans the full code exports to your GitHub repository.

faq_plan.q: How many people need to answer screening survey questions to fill a study?
faq_plan.a: Divide the completes you need by the share of starters you expect to qualify. For 150 completes at an expected 1 in 4, plan on at least 600 starts. Send a small first batch, read the real incidence rate, and adjust the invite list before the full send. Emergent puts no cap on survey responses, screen-outs included.

faq_plan.q: Can I ask screening survey questions when new users sign up?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Two or three questions at the end of an onboarding survey, such as role and how often someone uses the product, tag new users who fit a future study. Ask permission to contact them in the same step, and invite only people who agreed. In an app Emergent builds, every answer lands in a database you own, and the research list grows with each signup.
